summary.name: DisplayBuddy
summary.one_liner: A Mac menu bar app that controls external monitor brightness, volume, and inputs over DDC, with sync, presets, and schedules.
use_cases: Dimming an external monitor at night
Switching monitor inputs from the menu bar
Using Mac keyboard brightness keys on external monitors
Automating display settings when docking or at sunset
Controlling LG webOS or Samsung Tizen smart monitors over Wi-Fi
summary.what_it_does: DisplayBuddy controls external monitor brightness, contrast, volume, and input source from the Mac menu bar. It sends DDC commands to the monitor for hardware brightness control and falls back to gamma control if a display refuses DDC. Sync mode links displays so one slider adjusts all of them. Presets save and restore multi-display setups, and schedules tie presets to sunrise, sunset, time of day, charger, or a connected display. The page also mentions Wi-Fi control for LG webOS and Samsung Tizen smart monitors, Mac keyboard brightness key mapping, and macOS Shortcuts, Siri, a CLI, and MCP support.
notable: Sends DDC commands for real hardware brightness control, with automatic gamma fallback
Wi-Fi control for LG webOS and Samsung Tizen smart monitors
Presets and schedules tied to sunrise, sunset, charger, or connected display
caveats: Buy-once purchase; refunds available within 7 days on full-price purchases only
Platform named on the page is macOS only; Windows is not mentioned despite the title
Mac Apple chip support is stated as M1 through M5
